reason: E3 directly supports that laser cladding can produce TiC composite coatings on Ti6Al4V and that such coatings can achieve high hardness and improved tribological properties, though it also notes wear resistance can decrease with TiC content. E1 shows that hard phases in a coating improve hardness and wear resistance, but it concerns a different material system (HEA/WC) and notes non-uniform distribution. E2 is about a bulk refractory high-entropy alloy and provides no evidence for TiC coatings or their properties. Thus, the core premise of hardness/wear improvement by TiC is partly supported,
premises: Laser cladding can deposit TiC-reinforced composite coatings on Ti6Al4V
TiC particles in a coating increase surface hardness
TiC particles in a coating improve wear resistance
Uniform dispersion of TiC is achievable and necessary for the predicted benefits
